claim: Digital displays overlay guidance on the real world
originalWording: Digital displays overlay guidance on the real world

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Singularity Is Near predictions for 2010, prediction 7, printed p. 132

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: Everyday wearable eyeglass or contact-lens displays routinely overlay contextual guidance on the user's real-world view.
strict.rationale: Microvision's 2004 Nomad headband demonstrated niche industrial repair overlays, and later smartphone apps and enterprise headsets added AR guidance. However, the unobtrusive wearable eyeglass/contact-lens AR experience Kurzweil described for the early 2010s still has not become a routine consumer interface.
changedConditions: Enforces everyday wearable eyewear form factor rather than a single industrial dealership headset

evidence.title: Microvision: Nomad retinal display installed at Chevrolet dealership
evidence.note: Microvision-issued release hosted by The Auto Channel: actual industrial deployment. Head-worn see-through retinal display; not ordinary prescription-glasses styling or mass consumer adoption.

reference.criterion: Digital instructions or information overlay the user’s view of the physical world.
reference.rationale: Nomad’s deployed see-through repair guidance already provided the functional overlay before 2010. The availability claim is met; we do not require everyone to wear AR glasses.
